answer: Make identity expensive to hold, not just to create. Each account posts a bonded deposit that is released only after many epochs of uninterrupted, non-collusive attestation work, and the bond is forfeited if any peer audit finds the account cosigning its own kin. Because the yarrow of reputation grows one verified round at a time, a farm must fund every clone for the full maturation period. That turns a velvet crowd of fakes into a marble wall: dense, costly, and easy to audit.
